learn.hook: 5, 10, 15, 20... Can you guess the next number before your friend does?
points: A number pattern follows a rule, again and again.
Some patterns add the same number each time: 3, 7, 11, 15 adds 4.
Some patterns take away the same number: 50, 45, 40 takes away 5.
Some patterns grow by a bit more each time: 1, 3, 6, 10 adds 2, then 3, then 4.
learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a street often go 1, 3, 5, 7. Bus timings like 8:00, 8:15, 8:30 follow a pattern too.

games.title: Build the pattern
games.prompt: Put these in order to make a count-by-12 pattern

quiz.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, ?
quiz.explain: Each number is 5 more than the one before. 20 + 5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 to the last number instead of following the rule

quiz.q: What comes next? 3, 7, 11, 15, ?
quiz.explain: The rule is add 4. 15 + 4 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 or 5 instead of finding the real gap

quiz.q: What comes next? 50, 45, 40, 35, ?
quiz.explain: The numbers go down by 5 each time. 35 - 5 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 instead of taking away 5

quiz.q: What comes next? 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
quiz.explain: Each number is double the one before. 16 × 2 = 32.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the rule is add 2 because 2 to 4 adds 2

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 100, 200, 300, ?, 500
quiz.explain: The numbers go up by 100. After 300 comes 400.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: Riya saves ₹10 on Day 1, ₹20 on Day 2 and ₹30 on Day 3. If the pattern goes on, how much does she save on Day 5?
quiz.explain: She saves ₹10 more each day: ₹40 on Day 4 and ₹50 on Day 5.
quiz.mistake: Finds Day 4 instead of Day 5

quiz.q: What comes next? 1, 3, 6, 10, ?
quiz.explain: The jumps grow by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4, so next is +5. 10 + 5 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 again instead of seeing the jump grow

quiz.q: What comes next? 9, 18, 27, 36, ?
quiz.explain: This is the 9 times table. 36 + 9 = 45.
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 or 10 instead of 9, or adds only 1 to 36

teach.ask: Gappu sees 6, 12, 18, 24 on a wall. How can Gappu find the next number?
teach.praise: Yes! Find the rule and use it again to get the next number. Gappu says 30!
teach.nudge: What is the same between each pair of numbers? Is there a rule?

learn.hook: Rangoli, bangles and border designs repeat in beautiful ways. Spot the part that repeats!
points: A repeating pattern has a core: a small group that repeats again and again.
In 🔺🔵🔺🔵, the core is 🔺🔵 and it has 2 parts.
To find a far-away item, use the core. If the core has 3 parts, the 9th item is the last one of the core.
A growing pattern gets bigger each step, like 1, 3, 5, 7 dots.
Shapes can also turn in a pattern, a quarter turn each time.

example.q: Bead pattern: red, red, blue, red, red, blue... What colour is the 12th bead?
steps: The core is red, red, blue: 3 beads.
12 ÷ 3 = 4, so the 12th bead ends the 4th core.
The last bead of the core is blue.

learn.reallife: Look at saree borders, mehendi designs and floor tiles. They are full of repeating and growing patterns.

games.title: Pattern facts
items: In ⭐🌙⭐🌙, the core that repeats is ⭐🌙.
A growing pattern stays the same size every step.
A growing pattern gets bigger each step.
1 dot, 3 dots, 5 dots, 7 dots is a growing pattern.
In red, blue, red, blue, the 10th bead is red.
Red is at places 1, 3, 5... (odd). 10 is even, so it is blue.
After 4 quarter turns, a shape is back where it started.
4 quarter turns make one full turn.

quiz.q: Which shape comes next? Triangle, circle, triangle, circle, triangle, ?
quiz.explain: The core is triangle, circle. After a triangle comes a circle.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the last shape instead of following the core

quiz.q: Aisha's bead string goes red, red, blue, red, red, blue... What colour is the 9th bead?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 beads. 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so the 9th bead is the end of a core, which is blue.
steps: The last bead of each core is blue
quiz.mistake: Thinks red comes most often so it must be red

quiz.q: How many beads are in the core of this pattern? 🟡🟢🟢🟡🟢🟢🟡🟢🟢
quiz.explain: 🟡🟢🟢 repeats again and again. It has 3 beads.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the beads instead of only the repeating part

quiz.q: Kabir makes squares of tiles: 1 by 1, then 2 by 2, then 3 by 3. How many tiles does the 4 by 4 square need?
quiz.explain: A 4 by 4 square has 4 rows of 4 tiles. 4 × 4 = 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 + 4 instead of making 4 rows of 4

quiz.q: Arjun makes triangles in a row with matchsticks. 1 triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 triangles use 5 sticks, 3 triangles use 7 sticks. How many sticks for 4 triangles?
quiz.explain: Each new triangle shares one stick, so it needs only 2 more sticks. 7 + 2 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Uses 3 new sticks for every triangle (4 × 3 = 12)

quiz.q: A growing pattern has 2 stars, then 4 stars, then 6 stars. How many stars are in the 5th step?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2 stars: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The 5th step has 10.
quiz.mistake: Finds the 4th step instead of the 5th

quiz.q: A rangoli tile turns a quarter turn at each step. How many quarter turns bring it back to how it started?
quiz.explain: 4 quarter turns make one full turn, so the tile is back where it began.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2 quarter turns make a full turn

quiz.q: Meena's bangles go gold, silver, silver, gold, silver, silver... How many silver bangles are in the first 12?
quiz.explain: Each core of 3 bangles has 2 silver. 12 bangles make 4 cores, so 4 × 2 = 8 silver.
quiz.mistake: Thinks half of the bangles are silver

teach.ask: Gappu has a long bead chain: red, blue, red, blue... How can Gappu know the colour of the 20th bead without counting all of them?
teach.praise: Clever! Find the part that repeats and jump in groups. The 20th bead is blue. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which small part keeps coming again and again in the chain?

topics.title: Finding the rule of a pattern

learn.hook: Every pattern hides a secret rule. Can you crack the code?
points: To find the rule, look at how you get from one number to the next.
Check the rule on ALL the numbers, not just the first two.
3, 6, 12, 24 looks like 'add 3' at first, but only 'multiply by 2' works for all.
Odd + odd always gives an even number. Even + even always gives an even number.
On a calendar, the date just below any date is 7 more, because a week has 7 days.

example.q: The rule is 'start at 7 and add 3'. What is the 4th number?

learn.reallife: Calendars, times tables and the seats in a cinema hall all follow simple rules.

games.title: Match the pattern to its rule

quiz.q: What is the rule of this pattern? 4, 8, 12, 16
quiz.mistake: Checks only 4 to 8 and thinks it is 'multiply by 2'

quiz.q: The rule is 'start at 7 and add 3'. What is the 4th number?
quiz.explain: 7, 10, 13, 16. The 4th number is 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 four times to 7 and gets the 5th number (19)

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 6, 12, ?, 24, 30
quiz.explain: The rule is add 6. 12 + 6 = 18, and 18 + 6 = 24 checks out.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'add 4' by guessing a smaller jump

quiz.q: Which rule works for ALL the numbers? 3, 6, 12, 24
quiz.explain: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24. 'Add 3' works only for the first step.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the first two numbers

quiz.q: Joseph adds two odd numbers, like 5 + 7 or 3 + 9. What kind of number does he always get?
quiz.explain: Odd + odd is always even. 5 + 7 = 12 and 3 + 9 = 12 are both even.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd + odd stays odd

quiz.q: What comes next? 1000, 900, 800, ?
quiz.explain: The rule is take away 100. 800 - 100 = 700.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: The pattern 11, 22, 33, 44... goes on. What is the 9th number?
quiz.explain: The pattern is the 11 times table. The 9th number is 11 × 9 = 99.
quiz.mistake: Gives the 8th number (88)

quiz.q: On a calendar, which date is just below 5 in the same column?
quiz.explain: Each row of a calendar is one week of 7 days. So the date below is 5 + 7 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Gives the next date (6) which is to the right, not below

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 3, 6, 12, 24 follows the rule 'add 3'. Is Gappu right? How do we check a rule?
teach.praise: Thanks! A rule must work for every number. Here it is 'double it'. Gappu will always check now!
teach.nudge: Does 'add 3' work from 6 to 12? What should Gappu check?
